key_insight: Y6 excitons are mixed Frenkel-charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, and their quenching is driven by short-range, delocalization-assisted transport rather than simple hopping.
engineering_relevance: These results give device designers a quantitative way to link spectroscopy to interfacial transport, helping optimize single-component solar cells and related non-fullerene acceptor architectures.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films near hole-transport interfaces.
Analytical hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer model fit to extract coupling, charge-transfer admixture, and system-bath interaction strengths.
Interpretation of quenching kinetics to infer transport length scale and mechanism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1 ps quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, supporting a short-range injection mechanism.
watch_item: The extracted microscopic parameters are model-dependent, so the conclusions should be validated across film morphologies, interfaces, and other non-fullerene acceptors.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
